test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 08 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: __________ was launched by the Government of India in 2020 to make the country and its citizens independent and self-sufficient in all respects.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan was launched by the Government of India in **May 2020** to make the country and its citizens self-reliant.
 
• This initiative aims to provide a stimulus package of **INR 20 lakh crore**, which is equivalent to 10% of India's GDP.
 
• The Abhiyan focuses on five main pillars: Economy, Infrastructure, System, Vibrant Demography, and Demand.
 
• The goal is to promote local manufacturing, boost local markets, and reduce dependence on imports.
 
• The package covers various sectors, including MSMEs, agriculture, and public health, among others.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **MSME Sector**

 
 
• Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) are the backbone of the Indian economy, contributing significantly to GDP and employment.
 
• Under Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan, the government announced collateral-free automatic loans worth INR 3 lakh crore for MSMEs.
 
• The initiative also includes a Fund of Funds with a corpus of INR 10,000 crore to provide equity funding for MSMEs.
 
• Revised definition of MSMEs to include larger enterprises and allow them to take advantage of the schemes.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture Sector**
 
 
• The package includes INR 1 lakh crore for the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund for farm-gate infrastructure for farmers.
 
• The government also announced INR 20,000 crore for the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) to develop marine and inland fisheries.
 
• Reforms to amend the Essential Commodities Act and promote barrier-free inter-state trade of agricultural products.
 
• Focus on improving storage and logistics to reduce post-harvest losses.
 
 
 
• **Public Health**
 
 
• The package allocates INR 15,000 crore to strengthen public health infrastructure in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• Emphasis on ramping up testing facilities, creating additional hospital beds, and ensuring the availability of essential medical supplies.
 
• Enhanced focus on research and development of vaccines and treatments for COVID-19.
 
• Support for states to improve their healthcare systems and prepare for future health crises.
